rows.notes: The study is explicitly labelled a review/perspective article (header 'REVIEW ARTICLE'; abstract describes a 'high-level review' of nanobubble integration in spaceflight food production). It reports no own experiment, data or model runs; all yield/quality effects of nanobubble-oxygenated water (e.g. 24% and 40% yield increases in cucumber and tomato) are cited from Liu et al. 2019 and Zhou et al. 2019. It also concerns nanobubbles in hydroponics/spaceflight systems rather than aerated drip irrigation in soil. No primary evidence, so Q2-Q9 are no.

Review/perspective article with no own data. Statements that oxygen/ozone nanobubbles generate ROS with bactericidal activity, remove biofilms, and could serve as an oxidizer/disinfectant alternative to phytosanitary products in hydroponics are drawn from cited work (Shiroodi et al. 2021, Liu et al. 2016, Zhang et al. 2022) and framed as potential ('could', 'may'). No own result on reduced pesticide applications under aerated drip irrigation.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The paper is a narrative review/perspective on nanobubbles for spaceflight hydroponic food production; it contains no primary data and does not study aerated drip irrigation in soil, so it cannot support either claim as primary evidence.
